newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania evicts Kinshasa diplomats over unpaid rent.
newsitem.headline: Romania evicts Kinshasa diplomats over unpaid rent.

text.p: Romanian authorities have evicted diplomats from the Democratic Republic of the Congo from their Bucharest embassy building, because around $1.4 million in rent has not been paid, officials said on Tuesday.
The Foreign Ministry said it was not involved in the eviction, ordered earlier this month by a state authority which rents out houses to diplomats assigned to Romania.
The diplomats from the former Zaire, now crammed inside their ambassador's residence, said they had written to reformist president Emil Constantinescu to draw his attention to their plight.

"We are trying to get organised as well as we can. There's not much room in here, but we try to manage given the circumstances," a Kinshasa diplomat, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters by telephone from his embassy's improvised headquarters in central Bucharest.
"This situation is a legacy of the ousted regime," he said, declaring confidence in the government of President Laurent Kabila, who toppled dictator Mobutu Sese Seko in May.

Mobutu had been a frequent guest of Romania's dictator Nicolae Ceausescu, before Ceausescu was ousted and executed in a revolution in 1989. Relations between Bucharest and Kinshasa have cooled since then.
"We count on the goodwill of the (Kabila) government to set things in order...but the Romanians' patience seems to have run short," the Congolese diplomat said.
The vast central African country's mission to Romania vacated its posh premises in a residential area of northern Bucharest on August 4.
The Romanian Foreign Ministry said the amount of unpaid rent amassed by the mission since 1991 was $1.391 million.
"There are also penalties for seven years in back rent, as well as big sums in overdue electricity, heating and telephone bills," the ministry said in a statement.

It said the Kinshasa ambassador, Musungayi Nkuembe Mampuya -- the longest-serving diplomat in the Balkan country, whose assignment began in 1983 -- had agreed to vacate the embassy premises and to move offices to his residence.
"Everything was fine before 1989...we had joint ventures with Romania, which used to import industrial diamonds and rubber from our country," the Congolese diplomat said.
